title: Looking for character generation advice
author: Boomboxbeats
selftext:
I’ve been coding a game with GODOT and Codex for some time now. I keep coming back to the same problem every time. 

My game is isographic top down and with out going into the details when I got to animate sprites of the player character his feet and top half of his body need to move independently. Think dual-stick shooter-type movement. He needs to be able to walk or stand in any direction with one animation while throwing any direction at the same time. 

Codex tried to build a leg only rig that got so messy and patched that there was no consistency between motions. lol t was stripping the legs from my character and pasting it in a layer that looked horrendous. I’ve scrapped my main character implementation so many times at one point he had no hands or feet because I was so frustrated. I’ve spent weeks of codex time trying to figure out a good way to polish this character and it’s just not happening. I’ve been using auto sprite for all my sprite sheets which I have gotten good results from but it doesn’t fix my issue. 

Thanks for reading id love any advice.

comments.author: noobgameslab
comments.body: Don't ask the model for a finished full-body sprite sheet. Make one approved 8-direction turnaround, choose a fixed hip cut/pivot, then generate/clean two matching sets: legs (idle/walk) and torso (idle/throw). In Godot, stack two AnimatedSprite2D nodes; pick the leg animation from movement direction and torso animation from aim direction. Keep every frame on the same canvas and anchor. You'll still hand-fix the waist seam, but you stop asking AI to maintain two independent motions at once.

replies.author: Boomboxbeats
replies.body: I get your point. It really wasn’t my decision per se. Codex decided chopping stuff up would work so I let it try and it was a nightmare lol.

comments.author: Kashmakers
comments.body:
What about Godot's bone system? You can use the animationtree to have him do one action (walk), while another action is active (aim). Just got to animate it in animationplayer, save both of them as animations, and then use the Blend2 in animationtree and blend them together.

This does require setting up your character in Godot as something with bones to control. Which is not bad for pixel art to be honest.

I got my character set up with the animationtree so it can do various things with their arms, but their legs are for movement.

But you need the two animations already separate; the arms and the legs. And they need to be bones so Godot can say tell which movement should override the bone.

replies.author: Boomboxbeats
replies.body: I think this is what codex was trying to do with the leg rig setup but it had so many clear masking issues from tearing up the art I scrapped it after spending days trying to fix it for every direction and animation.
